item.title: Sir Patrick Stewart, RIP
item.description:
Patrick Stewart, as Captain Jean-Luc Picard. (CBS) The great British actor Sir Patrick Stewart passed away on Thursday . While Stewart began his career as a stage actor and performed in many Shakespeare plays, he is best known for his portrayal of Captain Jean-Luc Picard, in Star Trek: The Next Generation . Thanks to his impressive performance, Stewart and the character he played became science fiction icons. Stewart brought extraordinary depth and perception to the role. And the character is an interesting contrast to the more instinctive and aggressive, less cerebral, Captain Kirk in the original Star Trek Series . Perhaps more than any other character, Stewart's Picard epitomized Star Trek's progressive liberal values: Enlightenment rationalism, technological optimism (highlighted by his defense of the rights of the android Data ), racial and ethnic equality, and commitment to peace…

item.title: Trump’s List of Alleged Noncitizen Voters in California May Be Filled With Errors
item.description:
The Trump administration’s bid to stop 20,000 “likely noncitizen” voters from casting midterm ballots in California appears to be based on a list that’s riddled with inaccuracies. Two data analysts at the University of California, Los Angeles’ Voting Rights Project found that over 40 percent of the people the Department of Justice has deemed likely noncitizens were not even on the state’s voter rolls in the first place, and many others are likely legally eligible to vote. The analysts shared the conclusion in a legal filing on Saturday . The Justice Department’s list was shared the day before as a result of the Voting Rights Project’s lawsuit with the Los Angeles-based Coalition for Humane Immigrant Rights (CHIRLA) against the Trump administration’s attempts to interfere in the election. item.title: Canadian Prime Minister Carney reports progress in trade talks with Trump days before U.S. midterms
item.description:
A Biden-appointed judge late Friday ruled that the Trump administration exceeded its authority by threatening to prosecute state and county officials who do not comply with its election integrity efforts. U.S. District Judge Trina Thompson barred the Justice Department and Department of Homeland Security from pressing local election officials to purge registered voters, withhold their ballots, or set their midterm ballots aside solely because they appear on a federal list of suspected noncitizen voters. The Trump administration has argued its efforts are motivated by stopping illegal voting by noncitizens. item.title: Dozens injured, at least 6 dead in Halloween weekend gun violence at nightlife districts across U.S.
item.description:
Shootings in four college communities over the weekend left three people dead and at least 29 others injured. Indiana, Delaware, Alabama, Illinois and Colorado police are each investigating shootings in crowded parties near college communities, according to police and university statements. Seven were hospitalized in Bloomington, Indiana, near Indiana University's homecoming, while the University of Delaware is still counting victims (six are reportedly hospitalized) and the Magic City Classic football game between Alabama A&M and Alabama State near Legion Field in Birmingham, Alabama, left at least one dead and eight wounded. In Bloomington, Illinois, eight people were shot near Illinois Wesleyan University, leaving a 19-year-old woman dead. A shooting in Boulder, Colorado, left one University of Colorado Boulder student dead and another critically injured. SHOOTING AFTER MAGIC CITY…

item.title: US Midterms: Democrats face leftward surge
item.description:
With Republicans likely headed for a good ol' fashioned ass kicking in next week's midterm election, it doesn't seem too premature to ask the next big question: What are the Democrats going to do once they have a congressional majority? The New York Times reports that Democrats will move quickly on four items that are "consensus items among their members that are basic enough to bypass time-consuming committee consideration and go straight to the floor." Two of those items are really good ideas: ending President Donald Trump's tariffs and ending the war in Iran (or ordering Trump to "seek authorization from Congress to continue it"). Both would restore proper congressional authority in areas where Trump has expanded executive power, with terrible results.
